article.Citation/Title: Gent, E. M., Bryan, J. W., Cleary, M. A., Clarke, T. I., Holmwood, H. D., Nassereddine, R. O., Salway, C., Depla, S., Statton, S., Krecke, J., & Morgan, C. J. A. (2024). Esketamine combined with a mindfulness-based intervention for individuals with alcohol problems. Journal of Psychopharmacology, 38(6), 541-550.
article.InterventionDescription: Single sublingual esketamine hydrochloride oral thin film (115.1 mg) or vitamin C placebo, administered day 8, combined with 2 weeks of daily mindfulness-based intervention sessions; research clinic setting.

article.Outcome: The article headers its Results 'Primary outcome: Engagement (psychological and physical) in MBI' and the Aims state the study set out to test 'whether esketamine enhances engagement in MBI... and whether enhanced engagement has any impact on alcohol-related outcomes' -- so engagement, not the alcohol craving/consumption findings, is the stated primary outcome. Alcohol craving and consumption are explicitly analysed as secondary outcomes ('Alcohol-related secondary outcomes...were assessed using the ACQ-SF-R... and the TLFB'), so per the boundary-case rule for trials whose only SUD outcome is secondary, Outcome is coded from the primary (engagement) result and the discrepancy with the SUD-outcome-eligibility basis is flagged here. Of the three psychological-engagement statistics reported for the same analysis (group main effect F(1,26)=6.88, p=.014; time main effect F(2,56)=5.47, p=.007; time-by-group interaction F(2,52)=6.45, p=.003), the group main effect is used as Outcome/SD/PVal because it is the single-numerator-df test of the trial's primary condition comparison (esketamine vs placebo) and is cleanly convertible; the 2-df interaction and the esketamine-arm-only simple-effects t-test (t(52)=-3.29, p=.002) are alternative candidates for the same underlying finding but were not chosen. This selection among three co-equal-looking statistics is a genuine judgment call.
article.SD: 'F(1, 26) = 6.88' is printed in the same sentence as the chosen group main-effect statistic (Results, 'Primary outcome: Engagement' paragraph: 'a significant main effect of group (F(1, 26) = 6.88, p = 0.014)'); degrees of freedom included in parentheses as required.
article.PVal: 0.014, printed immediately after the F-statistic in the same sentence (Results, 'Primary outcome' paragraph).
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=28, the full randomized and analysed sample. The CONSORT flow diagram (Figure 2) shows Randomized (n=28) -> Esketamine (n=14)/Placebo (n=14) -> Received allocated drug (n=14 each) -> Completed 7-day follow-up (n=14 each) -> Analysed (n=14 each), i.e., zero attrition after randomization. This matches the mixed-model group-effect error df of 26 (28 participants - 2 groups = 26).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: No a priori power calculation or sample-size justification appears anywhere in the article (described only as a 'pilot study' in the Abstract, with no target-N or power discussion). No adverse-event/safety/side-effect section, table, or explicit statement appears anywhere (Methods, Results, Discussion, Limitations all searched); CADSS/BSS/MEQ-30 are reported as subjective drug-effect/mystical-experience outcomes, not as a harms assessment, so 'harms' is not described. The remaining 12 elements are all explicitly described: objective (Aims), design (double-blind placebo-controlled mixed within/between-measures RCT), setting (Psychopharmacology and Addiction Research Centre, University of Exeter), eligibility (AUDIT 8-40, age>=18, fluent English, exclusion list), intervention/comparator (esketamine 115.1mg vs vitamin-C oral thin film, dosing and administration detailed), outcomes (engagement, mindfulness, craving, consumption, mood/well-being, subjective-effects measures all named with instruments), randomization (randomised 1:1, stated), blinding (double-blind design stated throughout), statistical_methods (a dedicated Statistical analysis section), results (fully reported with test statistics throughout), funding_coi (separate Funding and Declaration of conflicting interests sections).

article.BaseStatus: No DSM severity subtype or single validated severity label is assigned. Coded 'Moderate' as an inferential judgment: the sample is a near-even split between 15 participants meeting only the study's 'hazardous drinking' threshold (AUDIT 8-14) and 13 meeting its 'moderate to severe AUD' threshold (AUDIT 15-40) (Results/Participants), and group-mean AUDIT scores of 15.3 (esketamine) and 14.3 (placebo) straddle that 15-point cutoff (Table 1). Genuinely ambiguous between Mild and Moderate; Moderate reflects that roughly half the sample meets the AUD (not merely hazardous-drinking) threshold and the esketamine-arm mean sits at/above 15.
article.PercentFem: Table 1, Gender M:F = 8:6 in each 14-person arm; 12 female of 28 total = 42.9%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Table 1, Ethnicity mixed:White:Other = esketamine 1:13:0, placebo 0:13:1. Non-white (mixed+other) = 1+1 = 2 of 28 total = 7.1%.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, low-income eligibility, or public-insurance criterion is described anywhere in the article; the eligibility list (Participants) covers only AUDIT score, age, language fluency, BMI, blood pressure, and medication/psychiatric exclusions. Coded 0.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted at the Psychopharmacology and Addiction Research Centre, University of Exeter, UK (author affiliation and corresponding-author address). Coded 'NonUS'; actual country is the United Kingdom.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Recruitment was via social-media advertisement from the community (Participants), but the sample was narrowed by extensive exclusion criteria (psychosis/schizophrenia history, current SUD treatment, hypertension, BMI <16 or >35, ketamine-contraindicated medication, positive ketamine urine screen, withdrawal symptoms) and, per the Discussion/Limitations, 'largely consisted of hazardous drinking students' rather than treatment-seeking AUD patients. Coded 0 as a screened, non-representative volunteer sample.
article.Comparator: Comparator is vitamin C in an oral thin film matched in form to the esketamine strips (Methods, 'Drug administration'), i.e., an inert placebo rather than a dose- or active-comparator design.
article.Power: No power calculation, target-sample-size justification, or explicit under/adequately-powered statement appears anywhere in the article; the study is described only as a 'pilot study' (Abstract). Coded 0 (not discussed) rather than '.' because this absence is directly observable across the full text rather than merely unclear.
article.HarmsAssessed: No adverse-event, safety, side-effect, or tolerability section, table, or explicit statement appears anywhere in the article (Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations all reviewed). The only safety-adjacent content is (1) generic background on ketamine's safety profile from the prior literature in the Introduction, which describes the drug class generally and not this trial's participants, and (2) a procedural note that a 'medical doctor assessed participants' street readiness before they were discharged.' CADSS (dissociation) and BSS (bodily symptoms) scores are reported as subjective drug-effect/mystical-experience outcomes tied to the study's mechanistic hypothesis, not framed as a harms assessment. Because the article never states whether AEs were monitored or occurred, this is coded as the article being silent on safety (SafetyReported='N', HarmsAssessed=0) rather than 'no AEs occurred' -- per the cardinal AE-gate distinction, this is flagged as a notable reporting gap given a psychoactive drug (esketamine) was administered to hazardous drinkers with no accompanying harms disclosure.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N' -- the article is silent on AEs/safety entirely (see HarmsAssessed rationale).
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.' (never 'NA' per field rule) because no safety-assessment population is defined; SafetyReported='N'.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA' because no AE data of any kind is reported, so there is no arm scope to characterize.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Coded 0: BMI and blood pressure appear only as screening/eligibility criteria (Participants), and the pre-dose breathalyser check is a procedural safety gate rather than a reported outcome. CADSS and BSS are self-report subjective-experience scales (dissociation, bodily symptoms), not objective biomarkers, vital signs, or CO-level measures, and are captured instead under the mental-health/subjective-effects constructs; no physical or biological outcome is reported.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Coded 0: the WEMWBS is a general mental well-being scale (captured under MentalHealthChangeMeasured), not a dedicated quality-of-life instrument (e.g., WHOQOL, SF-36); no such instrument is used in the study. Judgment call given the conceptual overlap between well-being and quality-of-life constructs.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 1: 'physical engagement' (self-reported frequency/dose of mindfulness practice) is one of the trial's two co-primary engagement outcomes, an adherence/feasibility-type measure explicitly adapted from Banerjee et al. (2018) (Measures, 'Engagement').
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1: a formal mediation analysis (Results, 'Mediation') tested psychological engagement as a mediator of the esketamine-to-alcohol-craving relationship (paths a, b, c'), directly assessing a mediating factor.
article.Followup in months: Two horizons are reported: from baseline (day 1) to final follow-up (day 14) = ~2 weeks (0.5 months), and from end-of-treatment/drug administration (day 8) to final follow-up (day 14), which the authors themselves repeatedly label 'seven days post-drug' (e.g., 'a significant difference between pre-drug and seven days post-drug'; Figure 2's 'Completed 7-day follow-up'). Per the end-of-treatment measurement rule, the 7-days-post-drug (1-week) horizon is used: 0.25 months. This differs materially (roughly 2x) from the ~2-week from-baseline horizon.

config_proposal.note: Primary outcome (psychological engagement in MBI) tested via the group main effect, F(1,26)=6.88, p=.014, a single-numerator-df F cleanly convertible to a Hedges' g equivalent; direction=1 because the effect favors esketamine (the psychedelic arm) over placebo.
